title: What the Old Man Does Is Always Right
summary: A country peasant rode to market to sell or barter his horse. On the road, he traded the horse for a cow, the cow for a sheep, the sheep for a goose, the goose for a hen, and final...
keywords: what the old man does is always right
full_text:
A country peasant rode to market to sell or barter his horse. On the road, he traded the horse for a cow, the cow for a sheep, the sheep for a goose, the goose for a hen, and finally the hen for a sack of rotten apples!

In the inn, two wealthy Englishmen laughed at his foolishness and wagered a bushel of gold coins that his wife would beat him black and blue when he returned home with rotten apples.

When the peasant arrived at his cottage and told his wife of each trade, she beamed with love: "A cow? How delicious, we shall have milk! A sheep? Wonderful, we shall have wool! A hen? Splendid, fresh eggs! Rotten apples? Heaven be praised! I can make apple sauce for our schoolmaster!" And she threw her arms around his neck and kissed him.

The Englishmen paid the bushel of gold with reverence, declaring: "When love is complete, whatever the good man does is always right!"
moral: Unconditional love and trust in a marriage turn every mistake into a blessing of peace.
